summary.text:
The task is to judge the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY against the strongest specific alternative, using the chapter as evidence.
The book entry correctly identifies the primary referent in Matthew 15:24 as the scattered house of Israel mingled with the nations, which the chapter demonstrates through the Jacob-Israel-Ephraim typology, the scattering of Ephraim as seed into the nations, and the promise of regathering into one stick. This reading aligns tightly with the 15:24 context and the OT patterns the chapter derives, giving it stronger explanatory power than the common view that treats the Israel-specific application as merely a secondary or contextual note.

The secondary clause ("more generally, any unrepentant sinner") is also supported by the broader symbolic usage the chapter itself connects to the same imagery 1 Peter 2:10 and the fullness of the Gentiles. While the common interpretation rightly notes that Luke 15 and Matthew 18 supply the dominant general metaphor, the book's entry accounts for the specific Matthean reference and the chapter's detailed regathering motif without contradiction. Therefore the entry is the best-supported explanation among the supplied alternatives. 

PERSUADED

  "rationale": "The BOOK ENTRY’s distinctive core (lost sheep = the already-scattered northern house of Israel mingled among the nations and thereafter sought/regathered) is not the best explanation of the supplied evidence. That contrast is fatal to an identification of the lost sheep as people already mixed into the nations. The same delimitation appears in the parallel mission charge of Matthew 10:5-6. The broader Lukan and Matthean lost-sheep parables (and the OT “sheep gone astray” texts) likewise portray ordinary sinners or straying Israelites, not a technical diaspora-Ephraim referent. The chapter’s synthesis of Hosea, Ezekiel’s sticks, and melo-ha-goyim supplies an interesting typological overlay, yet it cannot neutralize the plain mission-scope force of the very texts that employ the phrase. The secondary gloss (“any unrepentant sinner”) is uncontroversial but does not rescue the unsupported primary identification. support_scope.description: Support for the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY only, never for the supporting chapter as a whole.

book_secondary_elaborations.description: Secondary assertions actually printed in the glossary BOOK ENTRY; exclude chapter-only claims.

unsupported_glossary_assertions.description: Material assertions actually printed in the BOOK ENTRY that the evidence does not support. Must be empty for FULL and nonempty for CORE_ONLY.

chapter_only_objections.description: Objections to applications or arguments found only in the supporting chapter. Preserved for later chapter review and excluded from the glossary scope ruling.
